summary.en: Trace shared objects, null, identity and value equality without treating Java references as C pointers.
summary.bn: এক অবজেক্টের একাধিক রেফারেন্স, null আর দুই ধরনের সমতা ছবিতে বুঝুন।

notes: Objects.equals is available since Java 7; the reference rules follow Java 17.

sections.title: Two arrows can reach one changing object
Declare a reference, then decide its target
Mutation moves a value; reassignment moves an arrow
Follow aliases, missing values and comparisons
Give missing values an explicit meaning
Identity and value are different questions
Reference rules do not need new syntax
Keep variables, targets and contracts separate

examples.title: Mutation through an alias
examples.explanationHtml: Both references reach one Cell. Its value becomes 8 and the identity comparison is true.

examples.title: Fresh objects with matching fields
examples.explanationHtml: Two new expressions create separate identities. Cell inherits Object.equals, which also uses identity here.

examples.title: A null guard
examples.explanationHtml: The reference holds no object. Testing it before field access avoids a NullPointerException.

examples.title: Mutate, then redirect a parameter
examples.explanationHtml: The first assignment changes the original Cell. The second moves only the parameter copy, so the caller still sees 7.

examples.title: Null-safe content comparison
examples.explanationHtml: Objects.equals handles a null first reference without calling a method on it.

practice.title: Alias update
practice.statementHtml: Input: initial and replacement values from -100 to 100. Create one Cell and a second reference to it. Update through the second reference and print through the first.
hints: Use assignment rather than a second new.

practice.title: Optional result
practice.statementHtml: Input: a flag 0 or 1 followed by an integer from 0 to 100. With flag 1 create a Cell; otherwise keep null. Print its value or Missing.
hints: Guard the field access with a null check.

practice.title: Mutating helper
practice.statementHtml: Input: a Cell value from 0 to 100. Pass it to a static method that adds one to its field. Print the caller-visible value.
hints: The reference is copied but the object is shared.

practice.title: Count identical neighbours
practice.statementHtml: Input: n from 0 to 20 and n integer values from 0 to 100. Create a fresh Cell for the first value. For each later value, reuse the previous Cell if its value matches; otherwise create a new Cell. Print the number of adjacent reference pairs that are identical.
hints: Only reuse the prior reference when the values match.

quiz.prompt: Which value remains shared after changing an alias field?
quiz.explanation: One object exists; the mutation through b changes the field seen through a.

quiz.prompt: Does parameter reassignment replace the caller Cell?
quiz.explanation: replace changes only its local reference copy, leaving the caller on value 2.

quiz.prompt: Does inherited Object.equals compare these Cell fields by value?
quiz.explanation: Cell does not override equals, so inherited equality compares identity and returns false.

quiz.prompt: Which action through a null Cell triggers NullPointerException?
quiz.explanation: A field access needs an actual object. Comparing reference values does not dereference them.

quiz.prompt: Can Java references be advanced with pointer arithmetic?
quiz.explanation: Java does not expose C-style pointer arithmetic on references.

quiz.prompt: How should two String values normally be compared for content?
options: With equals, after handling possible null
quiz.explanation: Equal length does not imply equal content; == asks about identity.

quiz.prompt: When does a == b hold for two object references?
options: Their classes have the same name
They refer to the same object or both are null
quiz.explanation: Identity equality has no automatic field-by-field comparison.

quiz.prompt: What does Java pass when a Cell is an argument?
options: A copy of the reference value
quiz.explanation: The copied reference can mutate shared state but cannot rebind the caller variable.
The utility treats two null references as equal and safely handles either null input.

quiz.prompt: What can happen to an object after its last reachable reference disappears?
options: It is immediately guaranteed to be destroyed
It becomes eligible for garbage collection
The next reference becomes a C pointer
quiz.explanation: Eligibility does not guarantee a particular collection time.

quiz.prompt: What does a shallow copy of an object-reference array preserve?
options: Independent deep copies of every object
References to the same element objects
quiz.explanation: The container storage is new, but its reference elements still identify the original objects.

quiz.prompt: Which guard checks null before an instance field access?
quiz.explanation: Short-circuit && skips the right side when the left is false; order matters.

quiz.prompt: What else must a value-based equals implementation coordinate with?
quiz.explanation: Equal objects need equal hash codes. The later Object lesson develops the full contract.

keyPoints.en: Aliasing means two references reach the same object.
keyPoints.bn: একই অবজেক্টে একাধিক রেফারেন্স থাকাকে aliasing বলে।

keyPoints.en: null means a reference reaches no object.
keyPoints.bn: null মানে রেফারেন্স কোনো অবজেক্টে পৌঁছায় না।

keyPoints.en: Calling an instance method through null causes NullPointerException.
keyPoints.bn: null দিয়ে ইনস্ট্যান্স মেথড ডাকলে NullPointerException হয়।
রেফারেন্সে == দিয়ে একই অবজেক্ট কি না দেখা হয়।

keyPoints.en: equals follows the class-defined equality rule.
keyPoints.bn: equals ক্লাসে ঠিক করা সমতার নিয়ম মেনে চলে।

keyPoints.en: Reassigning a method parameter does not reassign the caller variable.
keyPoints.bn: মেথডের প্যারামিটার বদলালে কলারের ভেরিয়েবল বদলায় না।

examQuestions.question: Draw the references before and after assigning b = new Cell(9) when b previously equalled a.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Initially both arrows reach one Cell. Reassigning b moves only its arrow to a new Cell. a continues to refer to the original object. No original field changes from this reassignment.

examQuestions.question: Explain why Java is pass by value even when a method changes an object field.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The argument reference value is copied into the parameter. Both values identify one object, so mutation is visible. Rebinding the parameter does not move the caller reference. Sharing an object is different from sharing a variable.

examQuestions.question: Distinguish identity, Object.equals and String.equals.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Reference == compares identity. The inherited Object.equals also compares identity. String overrides equals to compare content, illustrating that value equality depends on the class contract.
